newsitem.title: UK: Guinness 96 pretax profit 975 mln pounds.
newsitem.headline: Guinness 96 pretax profit 975 mln pounds.

text.p: British-based drinks group Guinness Plc reported slightly firmer than expected profit growth for 1996 on Thursday, at 975 million pounds ($1.56 billion), and said it saw signs of better demand and pricing in the U.S. spirits market -- its biggest.

Chairman Tony Greener told Reuters the company achieved overall price rises in spirits of 1.5 percentage points worldwide in the year, "and the climate is improving both in terms of pricing and in terms of scotch (whisky) volume's underlying rate of growth".
Analysts had predicted the profit would be in a range of 960 to 965 million pounds and the dividend of 16.1 pence per share was narrowly firmer than the average analyst prediction of 16.0.

"We are now seeing encouraging signs in our largest spirits market, the United States, where Dewar's and Johnnie Walker Red Label increased sales into retail for the first time in some years and our other premium brands showed continuing growth," the company said in a statement.
In brewing, Guinness said its worldwide activities "again showed significant growth in key development markets, with particular progress in the U.S..."
"The U.S economy, being strong, is very helpful although in Europe, progress remains slow and we do not expect a big consumer bounceback in Germany and France," Greener added. ($1=.6271 Pound)
